newsitem.title: USA: General Mills sees earnings growth in Q2.
newsitem.headline: General Mills sees earnings growth in Q2.

text.p: General Mills Inc said Monday it expects renewed earnings growth beginning in its second fiscal quarter, although results for fiscal 1997 will be moderated by recent decreases in cereal prices.

"While the impact of recent cereal pricing actions will moderate the company's overall earnings progress in 1997, we continue to expect the vitality of our domestic non-cereal businesses and expanding international operations to generate good earnings gains for the year," Chairman Stephen Sanger said in a statement.
Earlier, General Mills reported first quarter earnings of $0.80 a share before accounting charges, down from year-ago earnings of $0.86.
The company said earnings declined due to price cuts taken by its Big G cereals division.
In June, General Mills said price cuts would reduce full-year fiscal 1997 sales by $100 million and net earnings by $30 million to $35 million, or $0.20 a share.
The company said more than half of this earnings impact fell in the first quarter.
The company said the earnings impact in future quarters will be less, as reductions in promotional spending behind established brands take effect beginning in mid-October.
General Mills is the second largest U.S. cereal maker, behind Kellogg Co.

Sanger said first-quarter operating results excluding the effects of cereal pricing actions met the company's goals, and reflected the continuation of broad-based volume and market share momentum from fiscal 1996.

"Our worldwide unit volume grew four percent in the (first) quarter, reflecting continued strong levels of product and marketing innovation across the company," he added. "This volume momentum is continuing in September, which raises our confidence that General Mills will renew earnings growth beginning in the second quarter."
